name: VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System)

header.one_liner: India's indigenous very short range air defence missile; DRDO design; man-portable/vehicle-mounted; 0.5–6 km range; designed to defeat low-flying drones, helicopters, and cruise missiles.

at_a_glance.Target: Low-flying drones, helicopters, cruise missiles, UAVs
at_a_glance.Platform: Man-portable; can be mounted on light vehicles

what_it_is.prose: VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System) is an indigenous Indian air defence missile system designed by DRDO to provide point defence for army formations against low-flying threats including drones, helicopters, cruise missiles, and UAVs. The system fills a critical gap in Indian Army air defence, replacing older Soviet-origin systems like the Igla-M. The VSHORADS missile uses an imaging infrared (IIR) seeker for terminal guidance, with a range of approximately 0.5–6 km and engagement altitude up to ~3 km. The system can be operated in man-portable mode (shoulder-fired) or mounted on light vehicles for greater mobility. The programme is in the development/procurement phase, with multiple successful test firings reported. The VSHORADS is designed to be complemented by the larger Akash and MRSAM systems for medium and long-range air defence, respectively.

faq.question: What threats does VSHORADS address?
faq.answer: VSHORADS is designed to defeat low-flying threats including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones), helicopters, cruise missiles, and low-flying aircraft within a range of 0.5–6 km. It fills the lowest tier of the Indian Army's layered air defence architecture, complementing the Akash (short-range) and MRSAM (medium-range) systems.

faq.question: Is VSHORADS different from MRSAM?
faq.answer: Yes. VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System) is a man-portable/vehicle-mounted system with 0.5–6 km range for point defence. MRSAM (Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile) is a larger system with 50–70 km range for area air defence. Both are indigenous DRDO programmes but serve different tiers of the air defence architecture.

faq.question: What is the Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS)?
faq.answer: VSHORADS is an Indian-developed, man-portable very short-range air defence system designed to protect ground formations from low-altitude aerial threats such as helicopters, drones and loitering munitions. DRDO has carried out multiple successful flight trials of the system.

faq.question: What stage has VSHORADS reached in its development?
faq.answer: DRDO has conducted successful flight trials of VSHORADS, including three consecutive tests validating its performance. The system is advancing toward user trials and production, with the platform positioned as an indigenous alternative to imported shoulder-fired air defence systems.
